# StateTree

57 tools for State Trees: states, tasks, transitions, conditions, evaluators, considerations, parameters and bindings.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_consideration`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Attach a utility-AI consideration (any struct deriving from FStateTreeConsiderationBase) to a state's Considerations array on a UStateTree. Considerations rank selectable children by score (0..1) when the state's selection behavior is utility-driven (e.g. TrySelectChildrenWithHighestUtility). Friendlier aliases are accepted in addition to the full struct name: "Constant" -> StateTreeConstantConsideration, "FloatInput"/"Float Input" -> StateTreeFloatInputConsideration, "EnumInput"/"Enum Input" -> StateTreeEnumInputConsideration. Use set_consideration_property to set initial values like Constant.Constant or FloatInput.Input. Idempotent: re-adding the same struct-type appends another consideration (engine semantics; considerations of the same type are valid).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UStateTree |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state to attach the consideration to |
| `consideration_class` | string | yes | Struct name (FStateTreeConstantConsideration / StateTreeConstantConsideration) or alias (Constant\|FloatInput\|Enum Input\|...) |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, consideration_class, consideration_count, added, saved }`

## `add_evaluator`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Attach an evaluator node (by struct name, via reflection) to a UStateTree; evaluators are TREE-scoped (they live on UStateTreeEditorData::Evaluators, not on a state) and tick for the whole tree, so this command takes no state_name.  Idempotent: an evaluator of the same struct already present is not appended again.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `evaluator_class` | string | yes | Evaluator struct name or /Script path; must derive from StateTreeEvaluatorBase (e.g. "TestEval_A" from the StateTree test suite, or any project/plugin evaluator struct). |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, evaluator_class, evaluator_count, already_existed, added, saved }`

## `add_state`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a top-level state (a new SubTree, never a child of another state) to a StateTree asset, then compile and save it. Idempotent: if any state already has that name nothing changes and already_existed is true. Returns state_count, added and saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the new state, e.g. "Patrol"; the other state commands find states by this name. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, state_count, already_existed, added, saved }`

## `add_state_enter_condition`

*Additive.*

Append a new enter-condition node, of the struct named by condition_struct and with that struct's default values, to the EnterConditions of one state of a StateTree asset, then save the asset without compiling it; there is no undo step. Each call appends another node, so repeating it stacks a duplicate condition. A missing tree, editor data, state or struct, or a struct that does not derive from FStateTreeConditionBase, is an error before anything changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory. Struct names: list_condition_types; list them: list_conditions; set a field: set_condition_property; inverse: remove_state_enter_condition; a condition on a transition: add_state_transition_condition; check the result with compile_state_tree.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state that gets the condition; the first state with that name in a depth-first walk of the hierarchy is used |
| `condition_struct` | string | yes | Condition struct name or /Script path; must derive from StateTreeConditionBase (e.g. "StateTreeRandomCondition"); a leading F is optional |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, condition_struct, enter_condition_count, added, saved }`

## `add_state_task`

*Additive.*

Attach a task node (by struct name, resolved via reflection) to a state's Tasks list on a UStateTree.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state to add the task to |
| `task_struct` | string | yes | Task struct name or /Script path; must derive from StateTreeTaskBase (e.g. "StateTreeDebugTextTask") |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, task_struct, task_count, added, saved }`

## `add_state_transition`

*Additive.*

Append a transition from from_state to to_state on a StateTree asset (trigger OnStateCompleted, type GotoState), then compile and save it; each call adds another one. event_name only fills RequiredEvent, which matters with an OnEvent trigger: set that with set_state_transition. Returns transition_count and saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `from_state` | string | yes | Name of the source state, which owns the new transition. |
| `to_state` | string | yes | Name of the target state the transition goes to. |
| `event_name` | string | no | Gameplay tag stored as the transition RequiredEvent, e.g. "AI.Event.Alert"; a tag that is not registered is ignored without error. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, from_state, to_state, event_name, transition_count, added, saved }`

## `add_state_transition_condition`

*Additive.*

Append a new condition node, of the struct named by condition_struct and with that struct's default values, to the Conditions of one transition of a state of a StateTree asset, then save the asset without compiling it; there is no undo step. The transition is addressed by state_name and transition_index, its 0-based position in that state's list as get_state_tree_info reports it (transitions[].index). Each call appends another node. A missing tree or state, a missing or out-of-range transition_index, or a struct that does not derive from FStateTreeConditionBase is an error before anything changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory. Struct names: list_condition_types; set a field: set_condition_property with target_kind "transition"; inverse: remove_state_transition_condition; a condition for entering a state: add_state_enter_condition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state owning the transition; the first state with that name in a depth-first walk of the hierarchy is used |
| `transition_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the transition within that state (the index field of get_state_tree_info transitions); required |
| `condition_struct` | string | yes | Condition struct name or /Script path; must derive from StateTreeConditionBase (e.g. "StateTreeRandomCondition") |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, transition_index, condition_struct, condition_count, added, saved }`

## `add_state_tree_binding`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Bind a UStateTree root parameter (source) to a target node's input property (target), so the node reads the parameter at runtime.  The target defaults to a state Task, but target_kind selects any FStateTreeEditorNode list: enter_condition/consideration (on the state) or global_task/evaluator (on the tree) — the binding anchor (FStateTreeEditorNode::ID) is identical for every kind. Authors an FStateTreePropertyPathBinding in the editor data's property bindings (idempotent per target path — re-binding the same target replaces it); validate it resolves with compile_state_tree.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `target_property` | string | yes | Name of the target node's input property to bind (the binding target), e.g. "BindableText". |
| `source_parameter` | string | yes | Name of the root parameter to bind from (the binding source; add it with add_state_tree_parameter first). |
| `state_name` | string | no | Name of the state owning the target node (required for target_kind task\|enter_condition\|consideration; ignored for global_task\|evaluator, which live on the tree). |
| `target_kind` | string | no | Which node list holds the target: "task" (default) \| "enter_condition" \| "consideration" \| "global_task" \| "evaluator". |
| `target_index` | number | no | Optional index into the selected node list (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path: string, state_name: string?, target_kind: string, target_index: int, target_property: string, source_parameter: string, source_struct_id: string, target_struct_id: string, bound: bool, binding_count: int, saved: bool }`

## `add_state_tree_global_task`

*Additive.*

Attach a global task node (by struct name, via reflection) to a UStateTree; global tasks run for the whole tree's lifetime.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree |
| `task_struct` | string | yes | Task struct name or /Script path; must derive from StateTreeTaskBase (e.g. "StateTreeDebugTextTask") |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, task_struct, global_task_count, added, saved }`

## `add_state_tree_parameter`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a typed parameter to the root parameter bag of a StateTree asset (the parameters that bindings and per-component overrides read), in one undo step, then save the asset without compiling it. Idempotent: when the tree already has a parameter of that name (case-insensitive) and type, nothing is changed or saved and the reply says added false and already_existed true; the same name with another type is an error and nothing changes. parameter_name is the name in the tree. A missing tree or editor data is an error; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory. Set its value with set_state_tree_parameter; inverse: remove_state_tree_parameter; bind it with add_state_tree_binding; per-actor values: set_state_tree_component_parameter_override.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Name of the parameter to add, e.g. "Speed"; a name already in the bag, compared case-insensitively, is never added a second time. |
| `parameter_type` | string | no | Scalar type: bool, int (default), int64, float, double, name, string, text, byte; case is ignored, int32 and fstring are accepted as aliases, and an unrecognised type silently becomes a string parameter |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, parameter_name, parameter_type, parameter_count, added, already_existed, saved, note? }`

## `compile_state_tree`

*Destructive.*

Compile a UStateTree via the editor subsystem (validate + compile); reports success and error/warning counts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, compiled, error_count, warning_count, message_count, saved }`

## `create_state_tree`

*Additive.*

Create a StateTree asset at package_path/tree_name (or load the one already there), giving it any missing editor data, the plugin UMCPStateTreeSchema when it has no schema and a Root state when it has no states, then compile and save it. Returns tree_path, state_count, created and saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_name` | string | yes | Asset name without path, e.g. "ST_Guard"; an asset of another class with that name is an error. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/AI" (default /Game/MCP). |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, tree_name, state_count, created, saved }`

## `get_component_state_tree_path`

*Read-only.*

Read which StateTree asset the UStateTreeComponent of an editor-world actor runs (its StateTreeRef), without changing anything. The actor is the first whose object name or editor label matches; an actor with no StateTreeComponent gives has_state_tree_component false and an empty state_tree_path, and a component with no tree bound an empty path. Bind or override with set_state_tree_component_parameter_override.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_label` | string | yes | Editor label or object name of the actor to inspect |

**Returns:** `{ actor_label, has_state_tree_component, component_name?, state_tree_path }`

## `get_condition_info`

*Read-only.*

Dump one condition node of a StateTree state as JSON without changing the asset: an enter condition of the state or, with target_kind "transition", a condition of one of its transitions. Returns class, instance_id and properties, the node struct fields (instance data is not included).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state that owns the condition; the command fails without it. |
| `condition_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the selected condition list, as counted by list_conditions or get_state_tree_info (transitions[].condition_count). |
| `target_kind` | string | no | Which list to read: "state" (default, the state EnterConditions) or "transition" (the Conditions of transition transition_index); any other value reads the enter conditions. |
| `transition_index` | number | no | 0-based index into the state transitions; required when target_kind is "transition" and ignored otherwise. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, target_kind, transition_index, condition_index, class, instance_id, properties: {...} }`

## `get_condition_property`

*Read-only.*

Read one property of a condition node on a StateTree state by reflection, without changing the asset: an enter condition (condition_index), or with target_kind "transition" a condition of transition transition_index. Use it instead of get_properties, which cannot address a node inside a state's condition arrays. Returns the value as JSON with its C++ type and has_value; only node struct properties are reachable, not instance data. Whole node: get_condition_info; write: set_condition_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state that owns the condition; the command fails without it. |
| `property` | string | yes | Name of a property on the condition node struct, e.g. "bInvert" on a compare condition; case-insensitive. |
| `target_kind` | string | no | Which list holds the condition: "state" (default, EnterConditions) or "transition" (Conditions of transition transition_index); any other value means "state". |
| `condition_index` | number | no | 0-based index into the selected condition list; omitting it fails as out of range. |
| `transition_index` | number | no | 0-based index into the state transitions; used only when target_kind is "transition", where omitting it fails. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, target_kind, transition_index, condition_index, property, type, value, has_value }`

## `get_state_tree_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the whole structure of a StateTree asset without changing it, as it is in memory (unsaved edits included), or one state's subtree when root_state is given. states has one entry per state, depth-first with the last top-level state first, giving its type, selection behavior, task completion, parent, depth and task, enter-condition, child and transition counts; transitions has one entry per transition with from_state, its index within that state (what the transition commands take), to_state, trigger, priority, event tag, condition count, delay and enabled -- filter it by from_state for one state's transitions; parameters gives each root parameter's type, or its class, struct or enum name, and its value_type. The root_state field of the reply is the first top-level state, empty when there is none. A tree that cannot be loaded or has no editor data, or a root_state that names no state, is an error. One state's nodes: list_tasks, list_conditions, list_considerations; finding trees: list_state_trees; compile check: validate_state_tree.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `root_state` | string | no | Optional state name (the first match in a depth-first walk, case-insensitive): states and transitions, and their counts, then cover only that state, at depth 0, and its descendants. Omitted, the whole tree. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_count, states: [{ name, type, selection_behavior, completion, parent, depth, task_count, enter_condition_count, children, transitions }], transition_count, transitions: [{ from_state, index, to_state, trigger, priority, event_tag, condition_count, delay, delay_duration, enabled }], evaluator_count, global_task_count, binding_count, parameter_count, parameters: [{ name, type, value_type }], root_state }`

## `get_state_tree_theme_colors`

## `get_task_info`

*Read-only.*

Read one task of a named state in a StateTree asset without changing it: the task node's struct name (class), its instance_id and every property of the node struct as JSON (properties). The task's instance data is not included. Errors when the tree, its editor data or the state is missing, or task_index is out of range; state_name picks the first state with that name. List a state's tasks with list_tasks; read or write one field with get_task_property or set_task_property; global tasks: list_state_tree_global_tasks.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state. |
| `task_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into State->Tasks. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, task_index, class, instance_id, properties: {...} }`

## `list_considerations`

*Read-only.*

List the utility considerations of one state of a StateTree asset without changing it: count and, per consideration in array order, its index, class (the consideration struct name) and instance_id (the node GUID). A state with none gives count 0 and an empty list; a missing tree, editor data or state is an error. index is what get_consideration_info, get_consideration_property, set_consideration_property and remove_consideration take; add one with add_consideration. Other node lists of a state: list_tasks, list_conditions (enter conditions); tree-scoped nodes: list_evaluators, list_state_tree_global_tasks; every count at once: get_state_tree_info.

| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state; the first state with that name in a depth-first walk of the hierarchy is used. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, count, considerations: [{ index, class, instance_id }] }`

## `remove_consideration`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a consideration (by index) from a state. Idempotent at the index-out-of-range boundary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state. |
| `consideration_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the state's Considerations array. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, consideration_index, removed, remaining, saved }`

## `remove_evaluator`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a tree-scoped evaluator (by index). Idempotent at the index-out-of-range boundary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `evaluator_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the tree's Evaluators array. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, evaluator_index, removed, remaining, saved }`

## `remove_state`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a state from the tree by name.  Idempotent: removing a non-existent state returns removed:false with a note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state to remove. |
| `with_descendants` | boolean | no | When true (default), also removes all child states recursively. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, removed, with_descendants, remaining_top_level, note }`

## `remove_state_enter_condition`

*Destructive.*

Remove one enter condition, by index, from a state of a StateTree asset and save the asset. An out-of-range index removes nothing and still succeeds, with removed false and a note. Returns removed, remaining and saved; for transition conditions use remove_state_transition_condition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state that owns the condition; the command fails without it. |
| `condition_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the state EnterConditions, as listed by list_conditions. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, condition_index, removed, remaining, saved, note }`

## `remove_state_transition`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a transition (by index) from a state. Idempotent at the index-out-of-range boundary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state. |
| `transition_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the state's Transitions array. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, transition_index, removed, remaining, saved }`

## `remove_state_transition_condition`

*Destructive.*

Remove one condition, by index, from a transition of a StateTree state and save the asset. An out-of-range transition_index is an error; an out-of-range condition_index removes nothing and still succeeds, with removed false. Returns removed, remaining and saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state that owns the transition; the command fails without it. |
| `transition_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the state transitions, as listed by get_state_tree_info (transitions[].index). |
| `condition_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the Conditions of that transition. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, transition_index, condition_index, removed, remaining, saved, note }`

## `remove_state_tree_binding`

*Destructive.*

Remove the property binding whose target is target_property on one node of a StateTree asset (and any binding to a sub-property of it), the way the StateTree editor clears a binding, then save the asset. Nothing bound there is not an error: removed is false and the asset is not saved. Returns removed, removed_count and remaining (bindings left in the tree); list them with list_state_tree_bindings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `target_kind` | string | yes | Node list of the binding target: "task", "condition" (a state enter condition; "enter_condition" also works), "consideration", "transition" (a transition condition), "global_task" or "evaluator". |
| `target_property` | string | yes | Property path of the binding target on that node, as list_state_tree_bindings shows it in target_path, e.g. "BindableText". |
| `state_name` | string | no | Name of the state that owns the target node; needed for the task, condition, consideration and transition kinds. |
| `transition_index` | number | no | 0-based index into the state transitions; used only by the transition kind. |
| `target_index` | number | no | 0-based index of the target node in its list, default 0; for the transition kind, the index into the Conditions of that transition. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, target_kind, state_name?, target_index, target_property, target_struct_id, removed, removed_count, remaining, saved }`

## `remove_state_tree_global_task`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a tree-scoped global task (by index). Idempotent at the index-out-of-range boundary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `global_task_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the tree's GlobalTasks array. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, global_task_index, removed, remaining, saved }`

## `remove_state_tree_parameter`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a named parameter from a UStateTree's root parameter bag. Idempotent — removing an absent parameter is a no-op (removed:false).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Name of the root parameter to remove. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, parameter_name, removed, parameter_count, saved }`

## `remove_task`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove a task (by index) from a state. Idempotent at the index-out-of-range boundary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state. |
| `task_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the state's Tasks array. |

## `set_condition_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one property of a condition node on a StateTree state by reflection and save the asset: an enter condition, or with target_kind "transition" a condition of transition transition_index. set_properties cannot reach it: the node is a struct in the state's condition list, addressed here by state_name and condition_index. Only node struct properties, not instance data. No undo step, no compile (compile_state_tree). The same value again gives value_changed false and still saves; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Read: get_condition_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state that owns the condition; the command fails without it. |
| `property` | string | yes | Name of a property on the condition node struct, e.g. "bInvert" on a compare condition; case-insensitive. |
| `value` | any | yes | New value as JSON: a number, bool or string, or an object for a struct property, applied through FJsonObjectConverter. |
| `target_kind` | string | no | Which list holds the condition: "state" (default, EnterConditions) or "transition" (Conditions of transition transition_index); any other value means "state". |
| `transition_index` | number | no | 0-based index into the state transitions; used only when target_kind is "transition", where omitting it fails. |
| `condition_index` | number | no | 0-based index into the selected condition list; omitting it fails as out of range. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, target_kind, transition_index, condition_index, property, set, value_changed, saved, new_value?, save_error? }`

## `set_consideration_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one property of a utility consideration node of a StateTree state (state_name, consideration_index) and save the asset. set_properties cannot reach it: the node is a struct in the state's Considerations list. Node struct properties only, not instance data. No undo, no compile (compile_state_tree); the same value again gives value_changed false yet saves, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Read: get_consideration_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state. |
| `consideration_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into State->Considerations. |
| `property` | string | yes | FProperty name on the consideration struct. |
| `value` | any | yes | JSON value to apply (any FJsonObjectConverter-supported type). |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, consideration_index, property, set, value_changed, saved, new_value?, save_error? }`

## `set_evaluator_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one property of a tree-scoped evaluator node of a StateTree asset (evaluator_index) by reflection and save the asset. set_properties cannot reach it: the evaluator is a struct in the tree's Evaluators list, not an addressable object. Only node struct properties are reachable, not instance data. No undo step and no compile (compile_state_tree). value_changed false means the value was already there; the asset is saved anyway, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Read: get_evaluator_property; indexes: list_evaluators.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `evaluator_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the tree Evaluators, as listed by list_evaluators; out of range is an error. |
| `property` | string | yes | Name of a property on the evaluator node struct; case-insensitive. |
| `value` | any | yes | New value as JSON: a number, bool or string, or an object for a struct property, applied through FJsonObjectConverter. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, evaluator_index, property, set, value_changed, saved, new_value?, save_error? }`

## `set_state_completion_type`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set how a state aggregates its tasks' completion (UStateTreeState::TasksCompletion).  NOTE: this is the tasks-aggregation policy EStateTreeTaskCompletionType {All, Any} (All = the state completes when ALL its tasks complete; Any = when ANY single task completes) — NOT a success/failed result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state to modify. |
| `completion_type` | string | yes | Aggregation policy: "All" (default in engine: Any) \| "Any" (case-insensitive). |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, completion_type, set, saved }`

## `set_state_selection_behavior`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set how one state of a StateTree asset is entered when the tree selects it (UStateTreeState SelectionBehavior: enter it, try its children in order, at random or by utility, or follow its transitions), in one undo step, then save the asset without compiling it. A state that already has that behavior changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false). An unknown behavior name, a missing tree or a missing state is an error before anything changes; a failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false with the change only in memory. The utility behaviors score the children through their considerations (add_consideration). Other state settings: set_state_type (its linked_asset_path links another tree), set_state_completion_type; read back with get_state_tree_info; check the tree with compile_state_tree.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state to change; the first state with that name in a depth-first walk of the hierarchy is used |
| `selection_behavior` | string | yes | One of None \| TryEnterState \| TrySelectChildrenInOrder \| TrySelectChildrenAtRandom \| TrySelectChildrenWithHighestUtility \| TrySelectChildrenAtRandomWeightedByUtility \| TryFollowTransitions; an EStateTreeStateSelectionBehavior:: prefix is accepted |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, selection_behavior, set, changed, saved, note? }`

## `set_state_transition`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Update any subset of the fields of an existing transition of a state of a StateTree asset -- trigger, priority, type, target state, event tag and payload, enabled flag and delay -- in one undo step, then save the asset without compiling it. Only fields explicitly passed are written; everything else is preserved, and the reply reads every field back. Every input is checked before any is written: an unknown enum name, target_state, event_tag or payload_struct, or a missing or out-of-range transition_index, is an error naming each bad input, and nothing is changed or saved, so errors in a reply is always empty. A call that leaves every field as it was changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false, a note). A failed save (for example while PIE runs) makes success false. A new transition: add_state_transition; inverse: remove_state_transition; conditions: add_state_transition_condition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UStateTree |
| `state_name` | string | yes | State that owns the transition; the first state with that name in a depth-first walk of the hierarchy is used |
| `transition_index` | number | yes | Index into the state's Transitions array (0-based, transitions[].index of get_state_tree_info); required |
| `trigger` | string | no | Optional EStateTreeTransitionTrigger name (None\|OnStateCompleted\|OnStateTick\|OnEvent\|OnDelta\|...) |
| `priority` | string | no | Optional EStateTreeTransitionPriority name (Lowest\|Low\|Normal\|High\|Highest) |
| `transition_type` | string | no | Optional EStateTreeTransitionType name (None\|Succeeded\|Failed\|GotoState\|Parent\|NextState\|NextSelectableState\|NextParent\|NextSelectableParent) |
| `target_state` | string | no | Optional re-target by state name (only when you want to redirect the edge) |
| `event_tag` | string | no | Optional event tag as a literal FGameplayTag string (e.g. "GameplayCue.Movement.Jumped") |
| `payload_struct` | string | no | Optional UScriptStruct name or /Script path for the event payload |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool (defaults preserved when omitted) |
| `delay` | boolean | no | Optional bool (when true, delay_duration and delay_variance are honored by the editor) |
| `delay_duration` | number | no | Optional number (seconds) |
| `delay_variance` | number | no | Optional number (seconds of random variance) |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, transition_index, trigger, priority, transition_type, target_state, event_tag, payload_struct, enabled, delay, delay_duration, delay_variance, applied_fields: [string] (the fields passed), errors: [string], changed, saved, note? }`

## `set_state_tree_component_parameter_override`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Override a single UStateTree root parameter on a UStateTreeComponent living on a placed actor. CRITICAL: the implementation calls UStateTreeStateTreeReference::SetPropertyOverridden(ParamGuid, true) — without this, the runtime reads from the asset default and the per-instance value is silently dropped. The value is written via FInstancedPropertyBag::SetValueSerializedString so the engine parses the string into the parameter's actual type (Bool/Int/Float/Vector/Struct/...). The tree must already declare the parameter; add it with add_state_tree_parameter first. Use clear_overrides=true to remove the override (asset default takes over again) without writing a value. If the component has no bound tree, pass state_tree_path to auto-bind before overriding (cold-start convenience); the public UStateTreeComponent::SetStateTree(UStateTree*) handles the bind through reflection on the protected StateTreeRef member.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_label` | string | yes | Actor label/name that owns the UStateTreeComponent (resolved against the editor world) |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Root parameter name to override (must exist on the bound tree); required unless clear_overrides is true |
| `value` | string | no | String-encoded value; type-driven by the parameter's FPropertyBagPropertyDesc. Required unless clear_overrides is true |
| `state_tree_path` | string | no | Optional path to a UStateTree to bind the component to if no tree is already bound |
| `clear_overrides` | boolean | no | If true, drop all per-instance overrides on the component (asset defaults take over); value is ignored |

**Returns:** `{ actor_label, component_class, parameter_name, parameter_id, value, was_overridden, cleared, saved, bound_tree }`

## `set_state_tree_global_task_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one property of an existing global task's node struct in a StateTree asset, by global_task_index, and save the asset; despite the name it adds nothing (create the task with add_state_tree_global_task). set_properties cannot reach a StateTree node, so use this; instance data is not reachable. The tree is not compiled (compile_state_tree). Returns value_changed, new_value and saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `global_task_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the tree GlobalTasks, as listed by list_state_tree_global_tasks; out of range is an error. |
| `property` | string | yes | Name of a property on the global task node struct, e.g. "FontScale" on a debug text task; case-insensitive. |
| `value` | any | yes | New value as JSON: a number, bool or string, or an object for a struct property, applied through FJsonObjectConverter. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, global_task_index, property, set, value_changed, saved, new_value?, save_error? }`

## `set_state_tree_parameter`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the value of an existing root parameter of a StateTree asset and save it. Works for bool, byte, int32, int64, float, double, name, string and text parameters; array and other types return an error. Add the parameter first with add_state_tree_parameter. Returns value_changed, new_value and saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `parameter` | string | yes | Name of a root parameter that already exists, as listed by get_state_tree_info (parameters[].name); an unknown name is an error. |
| `value` | any | yes | New value as JSON matching the parameter type: true or false, a number, or a string for name, string and text parameters. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, parameter, set, value_changed, saved, new_value? }`

## `set_state_tree_root`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Make a top-level state the root of a StateTree asset by moving it to the first SubTree slot, then compile and save it. A nested state is refused. Returns root_state with set and saved, or already_root when it was already first (nothing saved).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `root_state_name` | string | yes | Name of a top-level state, such as one made by add_state; a state nested under another is refused. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, root_state, already_root, set, saved }`

## `set_state_tree_theme_color`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Upsert a theme color in UStateTreeEditorData::Colors. CRITICAL: if a color with the same DisplayName (case-insensitive) already exists, its ColorRef UUID is preserved — state-level ColorRef references keep resolving, and the editor retains the original color identity in the asset's change history. Newly-created colors get a fresh UUID; the caller is responsible for re-binding any state ColorRefs that referenced an orphaned previous UUID. r/g/b default to 1.0; a defaults to 1.0. The engine stores Colors as a TSet&lt;FStateTreeEditorColor> keyed on ColorRef (display name uniqueness is the caller's responsibility — duplicate names are allowed by the engine but produce ambiguous lookups downstream).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UStateTree |
| `color_name` | string | yes | Display name (required, case-insensitive lookup) |
| `r` | number | no | red 0..1 (default 1.0) |
| `g` | number | no | green 0..1 (default 1.0) |
| `b` | number | no | blue 0..1 (default 1.0) |
| `a` | number | no | alpha 0..1 (default 1.0) |

**Returns:** `{ state_tree_path, color_name, color_ref, r, g, b, a, was_new, saved }`

## `set_state_type`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the type of one state of a StateTree asset (EStateTreeStateType: State, Group, Linked, LinkedAsset or Subtree), in one undo step, then save the asset without compiling it; with linked_asset_path it also points a LinkedAsset state at another StateTree. The state is the first one named state_name in a depth-first walk of the hierarchy. Without linked_asset_path only the type is written: the follow-up the StateTree details panel applies (clearing a group's tasks, resetting a link) does not run. With it, the engine setter UStateTreeState::SetLinkedStateAsset runs: it clears the state's tasks, takes the parameter layout of the linked tree and sets SelectionBehavior to TryEnterState, and the call always writes and saves. A state that already has that type, with no linked_asset_path, changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false). An unknown type name, a missing tree or state, a linked_asset_path with another state_type, or a linked tree that does not load is an error before anything changes; a failed save makes success false. Read back with get_state_tree_info; selection: set_state_selection_behavior.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state to change; the command fails without it. |
| `state_type` | string | yes | Enum value name: State, Group, Linked, LinkedAsset or Subtree (an EStateTreeStateType:: prefix is accepted). |
| `linked_asset_path` | string | no | Optional asset path of the UStateTree a LinkedAsset state runs, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Sub"; only with state_type LinkedAsset. |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, state_type, linked_asset (the state's linked tree, empty when none), set, changed, saved, note? }`

## `set_task_property`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one property of a task's node struct on a StateTree state (state_name + task_index) and save the tree. set_properties cannot reach a StateTree node, so use this; instance data is not reachable. value_changed is false when the value was already held (the tree is still saved). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. No undo step, not compiled (compile_state_tree). Read with get_task_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path to the UStateTree. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name of the state. |
| `task_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into State->Tasks. |
| `property` | string | yes | FProperty name on the task struct. |
| `value` | any | yes | JSON value to apply (any FJsonObjectConverter-supported type). |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, state_name, task_index, property, set, value_changed, saved, new_value?, save_error? }`

## `validate_state_tree`

*Destructive.*

Compile a StateTree asset in memory and report its errors and warnings without saving: valid, compiled, error_count, warning_count and the messages. It still marks the package dirty and refreshes the compiled data in memory; compile_state_tree compiles and saves.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the StateTree, e.g. "/Game/AI/ST_Guard". |

**Returns:** `{ tree_path, valid, compiled, error_count, warning_count, message_count, saved, errors: [{severity, message}], warnings: [{severity, message}], note }`
